trapezoidal.name: 梯形积分法
trapezoidal.description: Compute area at each level by pixel counting, then integrate area curve using trapezoidal rule to obtain storage curve. Suitable for regularly spaced elevation levels.
trapezoidal.monotonicity: Area curve is non-decreasing by construction. Storage curve is non-decreasing if levels are ascending.
references: Sawunyama, T. (2009). Estimating storage in reservoirs using remote sensing. IAHS Publ. 333.
Zhang, S. et al. (2014). Capability evaluation of retrieving reservoir parameters.

prism.name: 棱柱法
prism.description: Compute storage directly as sum of (level - elevation) * pixel_area for each inundated pixel. More accurate for irregular levels but computationally heavier.
prism.formula_storage: V(h) = sum(max(h - DEM_i, 0)) * pixel_area, for all valid pixels i
prism.monotonicity: Monotonicity is enforced post-hoc by taking cumulative maximum.
references: McFeeters, S.K. (1996). The use of Normalized Difference Water Index. Remote Sensing.

vertical_datums.warning: Public DEMs (SRTM, Copernicus DEM) typically use ellipsoidal heights (WGS84/CGCS2000). Water gauge levels may use local datums. Datum mismatch introduces systematic bias in absolute storage.

dem_vertical.impact: Directly affects storage volume. Propagates as: dV = A(h) * dh

water_level.impact: Affects both area and storage. Propagates as: dA = dA/dh * dh, dV = A * dh

water_boundary.impact: Affects area delineation. Mixed pixels at water edge introduce systematic bias.

limitations: Public DEMs represent post-impoundment topography and cannot capture original reservoir basin shape.
Sediment deposition alters topography over time; single DEM cannot represent multi-period bathymetry.
Water level and satellite image dates may not coincide exactly.
Mixed pixel effects at water boundaries cause area uncertainty.
Relative storage change is more reliable than absolute storage volume.
